shortDescription: Learn the principles of good design and the Adobe tools to apply them, from layout and colour to logos, social campaigns and packaging.
description:
This graphic design course teaches you both halves of the job: the principles that make a design work and the Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator skills to produce it.

Businesses across Nigeria need flyers, social media posts, logos, menus, packaging and brand kits every week. Clients notice the difference between someone who knows a few software tricks and someone who understands hierarchy, spacing, colour and type. You will build both, starting with how design works and moving steadily into real projects.

## What the graphic design course covers

- **Design principles.** Visual hierarchy, balance, alignment, contrast, white space, grids, scale and the Gestalt principles, plus style-scapes for agreeing a visual direction with a client.
- **Colour theory.** The colour wheel, analogous and complementary schemes, the 60-30-10 rule and why colours change between RGB screens and CMYK print.
- **Typography.** Type anatomy, leading, tracking and kerning, pairing typefaces, readable body text and fixing widows and orphans.
- **Layout.** Margins, columns, gutters, Z and F reading patterns and calls to action, applied to print and web layouts.
- **Photoshop.** The interface, layers, selections and masks, retouching with healing tools and Content-Aware Fill, natural portrait retouching, text and the Pen Tool, blend modes, brushes, actions and batch processing.
- **Illustrator.** Artboards, the Pen and Curvature tools, Shape Builder and Pathfinder, the Appearance panel, gradients, brushes, Image Trace and Live Paint, type on a path, variable fonts, envelope distortion, patterns and Puppet Warp, and exporting for print and screen.
- **Projects.** Logo design from brief to final files, a social media campaign, an infographic, food packaging on a dieline and a personal brand for your own freelance work.

## How the programme works

You follow a guided 12-week plan that sets weekly goals: a group of short video lessons, practice straight after each one and a quiz at the end of every chapter. Each quiz is drawn from the lessons you have just watched, and every answer comes with a short explanation, so a wrong answer teaches you something instead of just costing you marks. If your weeks are unpredictable you can learn at your own pace instead, though most learners finish sooner with the plan.

Quizzes cover both design judgement and software skill: why a layout feels cluttered, which blend mode lightens an image, what to send a printer for a poster. The projects are where it comes together, and each one gives you a finished piece for your portfolio.

## Tools you will use

You will use Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Illustrator, available through an Adobe Creative Cloud subscription (Adobe offers a free trial). A laptop or desktop is needed; a mouse makes precise work much easier, and a graphics tablet is helpful but optional.

## Who it is for

The programme suits creative people who want to turn an interest into paid work, marketers and small business owners who produce their own visuals, printers and sign makers who want stronger design skills, and anyone building a freelance design service. You do not need drawing talent: good design depends far more on structure and judgement than on illustration.

## After you finish

You will be able to take a brief, research the client, sketch ideas, produce clean files in Photoshop or Illustrator and deliver them in the right formats for print and screen. Your portfolio will include logos, social graphics, an infographic, packaging and your own brand, which is what clients and employers ask to see first.

## Certificate and final exam

When you are ready, you can get your SkillsAir certificate. Once it is unlocked, you sit a timed final exam drawn from every chapter of the programme. Pass it and your certificate is issued with a verification link that employers and clients can check. Certified graduates can also apply for internship openings from our growing partner network, with no job guarantees.

Every learner also gets the free Freelancer’s Academy bonus course, which shows you how to set up a professional Fiverr profile and gigs so you can start finding paying clients for your new skills.

faq.question: Do I need to be good at drawing?
faq.answer: No. Most graphic design is about structure, spacing, colour and type. Illustrator’s tools let you build precise shapes without freehand drawing skills.

faq.question: Which software do I need?
faq.answer: Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Illustrator. Both come with an Adobe Creative Cloud plan, and Adobe offers a free trial you can start with.

faq.question: Does the course cover CorelDRAW or Canva?
faq.answer: No. The programme teaches Photoshop and Illustrator, which are the industry standard. The design principles you learn apply in any tool.

faq.question: Will I have a portfolio at the end?
faq.answer: Yes. The projects produce logos, social media graphics, an infographic, packaging and a personal brand that you can show to clients.

faq.question: Will I get a job after the course?
faq.answer: There are no job guarantees, but you will finish with practical skills and a portfolio. Certified graduates can apply for internship openings from our partner network.
